title: Global Intelligence Monitor
summary: A one-page briefing on world news, conflicts, politics and the economy in the week to 10 November 2026 (Tuesday ~11:15 Europe/Rome), with country profiles and a timeline since 1945.

news.headline: Russia-Ukraine-US talks open in Abu Dhabi as Kushner calls for a 'new framework' for Europe
news.summary: Russian and Ukrainian negotiators sat facing each other with Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff at the head of the table. Kushner said the US hoped to create security relationships between Ukraine, Russia and Europe so as to end the war and build 'a new framework'; beforehand the Europeans, Ukraine, the US and NATO issued a joint statement reaffirming their commitment to a strong post-war European security architecture. The two-day round runs to 11 Nov.

news.headline: G7 foreign ministers reaffirm opposition to changing the status quo by force in Asian waters
news.summary: At their Paris meeting the G7 ministers restated their opposition to unilateral attempts to change the status quo by force or coercion in the East and South China Seas and the Taiwan Strait, agreed to counter market-distorting practices, arbitrary export restrictions and economic coercion, and condemned North Korea's nuclear and missile programmes. On Tuesday Ukraine's FM Andrii Sybiha met Rubio before joining a G7 session on Ukraine.

news.headline: Spain clears Ceuta port migrant camp; over 300 Moroccans return home in two days
news.summary: National Police resumed clearing the temporary camp in Ceuta's port, moving residents to other facilities or the El Tarajal CATE centre; local paper El Faro de Ceuta reports more than 300 Moroccans went home in two days. About 5,800 people still live in emergency facilities set up after an estimated 80,000 arrivals in late July; 14,818 have returned to Morocco since, 638 of them deported.

news.headline: Malaysian court orders Najib to begin house arrest immediately
news.summary: High Court judge Aslam Zainuddin set aside the 6 November order and issued a new one letting former PM Najib Razak, 73, serve the rest of his SRC International sentence under house arrest at his Kuala Lumpur residence until 23 August 2028, in line with the King's conditional pardon of 18 September, after the Attorney-General's Chambers had delayed his transfer.

news.headline: At least 10 killed in fog-bound motorway pile-ups in Bulgaria
news.summary: About 50 cars and trucks crashed on both carriageways of the Trakia motorway near Yambol in dense fog on Tuesday morning, killing at least 10 people and injuring about 27, the Yambol regional governor told BTA; the motorway was closed in both directions.

news.headline: France summons Iran's ambassador over supermarket fridge cyberattack
news.summary: France summoned Iran's envoy after blaming the Revolutionary Guards for the October hack that disabled refrigerators in hundreds of supermarkets; Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot warned Paris could respond with cyber measures of its own.

news.headline: Poland arrests two Ukrainians suspected of spying and sabotage for Russia
news.summary: Poland's Internal Security Agency (ABW) said it had arrested two Ukrainian men suspected of espionage and sabotage on behalf of Russian intelligence; Warsaw accuses Russia and Belarus of a hybrid campaign, which Moscow denies.

news.headline: European shares open near record high as oil slides below $91
news.summary: The STOXX 600 rose 0.9% to 662.54 by 0805 GMT, within 1% of its August record, with Germany, France and Italy up about 1% each, as Brent fell more than 2% to about $90 after Trump downplayed the need for military action against Iran; Infineon gained 3.1% on a 2027 growth forecast. Markets await US October CPI at 13:30 GMT.

news.headline: Board of Peace warns of escalating humanitarian emergency after Gaza floods
news.summary: Severe seasonal flooding over two days inundated tens of thousands of tents and makeshift shelters in the Gaza Strip, leaving displaced families exposed to cold and unsafe conditions, the Board of Peace said; WHO chief Tedros urged leaders to prioritise political solutions in Gaza.

news.headline: TPLF claims it killed 482 Ethiopian soldiers in renewed Tigray clashes
news.summary: The Tigray People's Liberation Front claimed (unverified) that its fighters killed 482 government soldiers and wounded 764 in renewed fighting in northern Tigray, contradicting the Ethiopian military's claims of victories.

news.headline: Europeans will be 'in the room' as Abu Dhabi talks open, says France's Barrot
news.summary: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot told Franceinfo that the UK, Germany and France will be in the meeting room for the Ukraine-Russia talks, and that there can be no discussion with Russia on European security before a ceasefire and peace; a Russian delegation source told Reuters Moscow sees a new European security framework as the main thrust of the talks.

news.headline: Israel issues tender for 732 settlement units in Gvaot, west of Bethlehem
news.summary: A Palestinian government body said Israeli authorities issued a construction tender for 732 housing units in the Gvaot settlement in the southern West Bank.

news.headline: Syria says it has not sent troops to Yemen
news.summary: Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani said Syria has no immediate plans to deploy forces to Yemen and that its military cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia does not include sending Syrian troops.

news.headline: Report: Israel and US negotiating a new multiyear military aid deal
news.summary: Israel's Yedioth Ahronoth reported that the two countries are negotiating a new multiyear military aid agreement; this is a press report, not officially confirmed.

news.headline: Japan to give the Philippines coastal radar and surveillance drones in $27m deal
news.summary: Under a 4.3 billion yen Official Security Assistance grant signed in Manila, Japan will provide a coastal radar to the Philippine Navy and surveillance drones to the Air Force, its largest OSA project so far and the first transfer of defence equipment under the programme; quantities and delivery dates were not disclosed.

news.headline: EU report: covert Russian network exploited October riots in France
news.summary: An internal EU assessment seen by Reuters says a covert Russian network used social media to blame the riots on uncontrolled immigration; a separate French foreign ministry assessment found accounts linked to Israel and the US MAGA movement also pushed 'hostile narratives'.

news.headline: Judo champion Teddy Riner enters France's 2027 presidential race
news.summary: President Emmanuel Macron welcomed the bid, telling France 5 it 'can only benefit the country'.

news.headline: Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh and a drone over Eastern Province
news.summary: The coalition said on Tuesday its air defences shot down a ballistic and a cruise missile targeting the Saudi capital and another ballistic missile fired towards southern Saudi Arabia, and destroyed a drone over the oil-rich Eastern Province; civil-defence alerts in Riyadh, Abha and Khamis Mushait were later lifted.

news.headline: SoftBank posts ¥1.1 trillion ($7bn) quarterly net loss
news.summary: SoftBank Group reported a net loss for July-September, compared with a ¥2.5 trillion profit a year earlier when it booked a large gain on its OpenAI stake.

news.headline: Kim Yo Jong accuses UN chief Guterres of siding with South Korea after border landmine blast
news.summary: North Korean state media said Kim Jong Un's sister called Guterres's call for dialogue between the two Koreas 'prejudiced and irresponsible'.

news.headline: Bangladesh rejects passport request from ousted PM Sheikh Hasina
news.summary: Hasina, 78, who fled to India in August 2024, plans to return home in December from self-imposed exile.

news.headline: Australia's eSafety regulator rejects tech giants' censorship warnings over Digital Duty of Care bill
news.summary: The regulator argued platforms' business models push them to maximise engagement; the proposed law would force internet companies to proactively prevent user harms or face fines.

news.headline: Paraguay prosecutors raid ousted president Peña's home in Ueno Bank probe
news.summary: Prosecutors searched the home on Monday and sought international help to trace missing funds; Peña is in pretrial detention, while the new president looks to reshuffle his cabinet.

news.headline: Record 2.5 million attend Pope Leo's Mass in Buenos Aires
news.summary: On the first papal trip to Argentina in 39 years, Leo urged President Milei not to target the poorest and warned about unregulated automation; he travels to Peru on Wednesday and returns to Rome on 17 Nov.

news.headline: Death toll from migrant boat sinking off Senegal rises to 39
news.summary: The pirogue left Saint-Louis for Spain's Canary Islands and capsized near Kébémer on 8 Nov; only one person was rescued. President Faye vowed to crack down on smuggling networks.

news.headline: Iraq reopens Sheeb border crossing with Iran
news.summary: Iraq's Border Ports Authority said the Sheeb crossing with Iran would reopen on Tuesday morning after technical work, while the Mandali crossing will close temporarily from Friday, state news agency INA reported.

news.headline: Private plane carrying six foreign nationals crashes in southern Philippines
news.summary: A disaster official in Digos, Davao del Sur, said rescue operations were under way and it was not yet known whether the passengers and crew had been killed.

news.headline: Three contract workers die of asphyxiation at Tata Electronics iPhone-parts plant in Hosur
news.summary: The deaths at the Tamil Nadu factory, which makes parts for Apple iPhones, triggered investigations by the companies and the state government, the latest incident in Apple's Indian supply chain.

news.headline: Japanese investors turn net buyers of foreign bonds for first time in three months
news.summary: Finance Ministry data showed net purchases of 493.9 billion yen ($3.13bn) of foreign bonds in October, as Treasury yields eased from early-October highs and AI-stock selloffs boosted safe-haven demand.

news.headline: Rights group claims Houthi attacks killed 33 civilians in Taiz over 73 hours
news.summary: The Yemeni Network for Rights and Freedoms (aligned with the government side) claimed shelling killed 33 and wounded 58, including about 30 dead at Al-Hadara market in Al-Wazi'iyah; the Houthis and local authorities traded blame. Figures not independently verified.

news.headline: Trump says Iran war 'militarily effectively over' as Iran's Rezaei demands the US accept its seven conditions
news.summary: After meeting Qatar's PM, Trump said the war was 'effectively over' and renewed strikes 'quite unlikely', while the naval blockade and the new land-route operation Iron Gate stay in place. Iran's Mohsen Rezaei dismissed reports of bilateral talks as 'imaginary' and said the US must 'surrender' to Tehran's seven conditions.

news.headline: Merz nominates Ilse Aigner for German president
news.summary: Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced that the CDU federal executive backed his proposal to nominate Ilse Aigner for the presidency, which could make her Germany's first female head of state.

news.headline: At least 21 killed in bus-truck collision in Tanzania's Iringa Region
news.summary: Police said a bus collided with a cargo truck in southern Tanzania on Monday, killing 10 men, nine women and two children and injuring five others.

news.headline: US officials say Moscow and Kyiv show 'a little flexibility' privately on Donetsk as Abu Dhabi talks open
news.summary: On the eve of the talks a US official said both sides' public positions on Donetsk had not moved but they had shown some private flexibility, and that territory would not be settled before a postwar security architecture. The proposed framework includes security consultations, crisis hotlines, reciprocal de-escalation and possibly reactivating the NATO-Russia Council. Kushner said the talks could at most 'build momentum toward the next phase'.

news.headline: France blames Iran's Revolutionary Guards for October supermarket refrigerator hacks, vows consequences
news.summary: French officials said the IRGC was responsible for cyberattacks that knocked out commercial refrigerators and freezers in hundreds of French supermarkets in early October, among the most disruptive cyber incidents of the Iran war that began in February.

news.headline: China's October exports jump 35.2% and imports 41.6%; trade surplus narrows to $105.3bn
news.summary: Customs data showed exports beat the ~33.5% forecast (September: 36.3%) on demand for chips and AI hardware, while imports surged far more than expected. The surplus fell to its lowest since April, though the year-to-date surplus topped $1 trillion.

news.headline: Paraguay: 93.1% of covered Ueno Bank depositors have now been repaid
news.summary: The central bank said 1,738,804 accounts covered by the deposit guarantee fund have received about 2.126 trillion guaraníes (~$340m); some 128,000 accounts remain. The fate of balances above the ~$38,600 cap, including about $800m in state and pension funds, is still unclear.

news.headline: Zelenskyy welcomes India's offer to mediate Black Sea 'food corridors'
news.summary: After a call with PM Narendra Modi on the eve of the Abu Dhabi talks, Zelenskyy said India is ready to help mediate between Russia and Ukraine to establish food corridors.

news.headline: Japan's real household spending falls 6.8% in September
news.summary: Government data on Tuesday showed spending by households of two or more fell a real 6.8% year on year; separately Japan posted a September current account surplus of ¥2.37 trillion.

news.headline: Russia and Ukraine open US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi, first since February
news.summary: Two days of talks were set to begin around 0630 GMT on 10 Nov. Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky leads Russia's team, which includes Deputy FM Sergei Ryabkov for the first time; Rustem Umerov leads Ukraine's. Zelenskiy says battlefield gains strengthen Kyiv's hand; a US official says both sides may cede some territory, which a senior Ukrainian official denied.

news.headline: Massie files eight articles of impeachment against Defence Secretary Hegseth
news.summary: Republican Rep. Thomas Massie introduced eight articles accusing Pete Hegseth of illegally waging the Iran war without congressional authorisation and abusing his powers; the House could vote as early as 11 Nov, and some Republicans signal they may back the charges. Rubio defended Hegseth in Paris.

news.headline: IAEA: drone strikes kill Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant worker and a thermal plant employee
news.summary: The IAEA said a worker at the Russian-occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant and an employee of the nearby thermal power plant were killed in separate drone attacks on 9 Nov, the second nuclear plant worker killed in under two weeks; Rafael Grossi called the attacks unacceptable. The Russian-installed management blamed Ukraine.

news.headline: Netanyahu again calls for a unity government after Eisenkot gets mandate
news.summary: A day after President Herzog gave opposition rival Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form a coalition, caretaker PM Netanyahu said in a video that 'a unity government is, simply, a necessity'. Eisenkot's bloc won 48 seats and Netanyahu's 53 of the 61 needed in the 27 Oct election.

news.headline: Asian stocks close higher: Kospi +4.0% to 5,221, Nikkei +2.7% to 60,381
news.summary: Tracking Wall Street's best day since April and lower oil, the Kospi closed up 4.03% at 5,221.20, Taiwan's index rose 3.10% to 42,951.66 and the Nikkei 225 gained 2.73% to 60,380.50; the Hang Seng added 0.70% and Shanghai 0.32%. SoftBank jumped about 14-15% ahead of earnings; Brent traded around $92 a barrel.

news.headline: Trump revives election fraud claims after midterm defeat
news.summary: President Trump on Monday revived allegations of election fraud, reversing his initial acceptance of last week's midterm results after Democrats swept both chambers of Congress; the allegations are unsubstantiated.

news.headline: M. John Harrison wins the Booker Prize for 'The End of Everything'
news.summary: British author M. John Harrison, 81, won the Booker Prize for his novel 'The End of Everything', a darkly satirical post-apocalyptic Britain that echoes concerns about AI; he is the oldest winner of the £50,000 award.

news.headline: Leaked Rosstat data points to over 450,000 Russian war deaths
news.summary: A reported data leak from Russia's state statistics agency Rosstat indicates that, by official figures, more than 450,000 Russians have been killed in the war in Ukraine, with the rate accelerating; the war would be the fourth most common cause of death in Russia since 2022 (leak not officially confirmed).

news.headline: Boeing Commercial Airplanes to cut 5% of its workforce
news.summary: Division chief Stephanie Pope told employees in an internal memo that the unit plans to cut about 5% of staff as it struggles to raise jetliner production.

news.headline: Trump says no new US offensive on Iran for now, sees 'good chance' of a deal
news.summary: On Truth Social after meeting Qatar's prime minister, Trump said the US will not launch a renewed offensive for the time being, citing 'positive momentum' and Gulf allies' preference for the status quo; at the White House he said Iran is 'talking very politely'. Iran's security council chief Mohsen Rezaei told the US to stop 'manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks'.

news.headline: Honda to build $3 billion hybrid-focused auto plant in Ohio
news.summary: Its first new US mass-production assembly plant since 2008: capacity of 240,000 vehicles a year, more than 2,000 jobs and production from 2029, lifting Honda's US capacity to about 1.3 million vehicles.

news.headline: Trump tells Reuters Qatar and Saudi Arabia want a peaceful Iran deal; US 'ready to go' with strikes
news.summary: In a brief phone interview after meeting Qatar's prime minister, Trump said both Gulf states would rather see a peaceful solution but the US is ready to resume strikes 'anytime we want'; he signalled no rush, saying he is content with the US naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz.

news.headline: Japan's LDP disciplines ex-PM Ishiba over consumption-tax vote walkout
news.summary: The ruling party warned former Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba and three other lawmakers for walking out before a lower-house vote on a consumption tax cut bill; Asahi says it is the first time the LDP has disciplined a former prime minister under party rules.

news.headline: Malaysia: eight missing after water surge at Sungai Pertak, Kuala Kubu Baru
news.summary: A sudden water surge left eight people missing and nine stranded in three separate incidents; the Fire and Rescue Department has launched a search operation.

news.headline: CVC and GBL pass 90% of Recordati, clearing path to delisting
news.summary: The private equity firm and Belgian investment group secured more than 90% of the Italian drugmaker at the end of the takeover offer period, the threshold needed to delist the €11 billion company.

news.headline: SpaceX plans ~$24 billion gas power plant and data centre in Starbase, Texas
news.summary: A public hearing notice shows the request for a gas-fired plant and super-compute facility, as local opposition to data centres grows (voters rejected them in 40 of 41 local ballot measures).

news.headline: At least 20 migrants dead, 133 rescued in boat incidents south of Crete
news.summary: Greek broadcaster ERT reported a series of incidents; in the latest, a container ship spotted a boat about 15 nautical miles southeast of Kaloi Limenes and the coast guard rescued 18 survivors and recovered 12 bodies.

news.headline: White House briefly locked down after car crashes near Lafayette Square barrier
news.summary: The Secret Service said the driver, who crashed onto the sidewalk near 16th and H streets NW around 10 a.m. local time, was 'combative with law enforcement' and was quickly arrested.
news.source: Indian Express (citing Fox News / Secret Service)

news.headline: Iran defends two-day talks offer as Trump meets Qatar's PM
news.summary: Spokesman Baghaei said demands that US sanctions and the naval blockade be lifted first are reasonable, after Rubio called some conditions 'outrageous and ridiculous'. Trump was due to meet mediator Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani; US and Gulf officials see no imminent deal.

news.headline: Drone attack hits Iraq's Khor Mor gas field
news.summary: The attack on the Kurdistan-region field came at 23:10 local time on Sunday; no casualties were reported and PM Ali al-Zaidi ordered a joint investigation.

news.headline: Wall Street posts best day in months as oil slides; Nvidia falls
news.summary: S&P 500 +2.41% to 7,554.67, Dow +2.21% to 52,417.54, Nasdaq +2.67% to 25,235.49, rebounding from last week's post-midterm AI sell-off. Philadelphia chip index +6% (AMD ~+13%, Broadcom ~+9%) while Nvidia was the only decliner after its board opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang. All 11 S&P sectors rose.

news.headline: Bank of England's Bailey warns AI payoff may take longer than markets expect
news.summary: Speaking in Switzerland, Governor Andrew Bailey said the returns from AI 'take longer to be realised than predicted', citing Edison and electricity, and flagged the risk of an AI bubble. Brent fell 4.4% to about $93 after Trump said fresh Iran strikes were 'highly unlikely'.

news.headline: Pope Leo XIV urges Milei's government to protect the most vulnerable
news.summary: Visiting the Cottolengo Don Orione home in Claypole near Buenos Aires, which cares for over 400 people and has been hit by spending cuts, the Pope said a nation's progress should be judged by how it treats those most in need. Part of a 12-day South American tour.

news.headline: Storm Charles to bring torrential rain and 120 km/h winds to Portugal and Spain
news.summary: The depression is expected to worsen the weather from Wednesday with heavy rain, gusts above 120 km/h and rough seas; Madeira will feel the effects from Tuesday.

news.headline: FDA orders vision-loss warnings on GLP-1 weight-loss drugs
news.summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is requiring makers of GLP-1 medicines to update safety labels to warn of a potential increased risk of a rare but serious eye condition that can cause permanent vision loss.

news.headline: Steel plant blast in Turkey's Izmir province kills 17
news.summary: An earthquake-like explosion around noon (0900 GMT) at the Habas iron and steel works in Aliaga district killed 17 people, Euronews reported late on Monday; earlier the governor's office had reported 3 dead, 10 missing and 14 injured.

news.headline: High-rise fire in China's Taiyuan kills at least 14
news.summary: A fire on Sunday evening in a building on a busy downtown road in the Shanxi provincial capital killed at least 14; 25 people remain in hospital, nine seriously injured, Xinhua said.

news.headline: France blames Iran's Revolutionary Guards for October cyberattacks on supermarket fridges
news.summary: FM Barrot said after the G7 meeting that the IRGC was behind the 11-12 Oct attacks on refrigeration units at more than 700 French stores (Carrefour, Monoprix, Intermarché, U); Iran's ambassador will be summoned and France will seek EU sanctions. The ministry cites fires and losses of tens of millions of euros; the investigation is still under way.

news.headline: Merz: no extra Ukraine aid, no EU budget deal
news.summary: In a letter to Council President Costa, the German chancellor tied agreement on the EU budget to approving an additional €45 billion for Kyiv, calling support for Ukraine a matter of 'indivisible European security'.

news.headline: Ukraine hits Russia's second-largest refinery as fuel rationing spreads
news.summary: Three main processing units at the KINEF plant (about 7% of Russian refining capacity, supplier of St Petersburg's Pulkovo airport) were damaged. Rosneft separately capped fuel sales in six regions, limiting drivers to 30 litres per transaction in cities.

news.headline: European stocks rally on bank deals; Crédit Agricole proposes merger with Banco BPM
news.summary: Stoxx 600 +1.26% to 656.52, FTSE MIB +2.7%. Crédit Agricole proposed merging its Italian unit with Banco BPM (20% premium, €1bn special dividend), creating Italy's third-largest bank; Banco BPM +10.7%. UniCredit +6.3% after a 24% Q3 profit rise and higher guidance. Brent fell about 4.5% after Trump played down new Iran strikes.

news.headline: Ukraine, Russia and US resume talks in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 Nov; EU sends a joint team
news.summary: First trilateral round since February, led for the US by Witkoff and Kushner. Agenda: post-war security guarantees, de-escalation and humanitarian issues; NYT (via RBC-Ukraine) says a ceasefire is not on the agenda. The Commission and Council send a joint team, with France, Germany, the UK, Italy and NATO also present; analysts expect no breakthrough.

news.headline: Beijing 'in communication' on a possible Trump-Xi-Putin meeting at APEC in Shenzhen
news.summary: Trump said he will likely meet Xi and Putin in a rare three-way meeting on the sidelines of APEC (18-19 Nov); China said on Monday it was in contact with the relevant parties and did not rule it out. Not confirmed.

news.headline: G7 foreign ministers meet in Paris and press Rubio on Iran and Ukraine
news.summary: Two-day meeting (9-10 Nov). European ministers want Ukraine and Europe included in any US-Russia settlement and favour diplomacy with Iran; Rubio's first trip since the midterms.

news.headline: COP31 climate conference opens in Antalya
news.summary: UN climate talks run 9-20 Nov in Turkey with more than 100,000 people expected; financial constraints and geopolitical tensions complicate cooperation.

news.headline: Russell Brand jailed for 10 years and six months
news.summary: Sentenced at Southwark Crown Court for one rape and three sexual assaults.

news.headline: Asian stocks rebound on chipmakers; Brent slips below $100
news.summary: Saxo: Taiex about +5%, Nikkei about +2.5% in Monday afternoon trade, TSMC +5.6%. Brent about $96.80 (-1.5%) after a ~16% weekly fall, gold ~$4,122. US October CPI is due Tuesday.

news.headline: Trump: Ukraine may end up 'a little bit different shape'
news.summary: In a CBS '60 Minutes' interview Trump said the war would end soon and suggested altered borders; Rubio said some progress has been made on post-war security arrangements.

news.headline: Trump says new Iran strikes 'highly unlikely' if talks progress
news.summary: Told CNN it 'depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement' on the nuclear programme and Hormuz, while saying three carriers are in the region and 38 bridges are in US sights. Both sides reported ships hit near Hormuz; Iran's foreign minister warned Tehran would 'rain down hell' if the US chooses war.

news.headline: Herzog tasks Gadi Eisenkot with forming Israel's next government
news.summary: Eisenkot (Yashar) had 67 recommendations against 46 for Netanyahu and has 28 days, extendable by 14. He pledged a 'national emergency government'.

news.headline: Houthi missiles intercepted over Riyadh; debris damages Aramco tower
news.summary: Saudi air defences intercepted missiles; falling debris caused limited damage to Aramco's building in the King Abdullah Financial District, no injuries reported. The Houthis claimed hits on King Khalid airport and oil facilities (claim).

news.headline: Egypt train collision in Giza kills seven
news.summary: A Giza-Fayoum train hit the rear of a stationary Cairo-Aswan train in al-Ayyat; 114-125 injured according to different counts. Investigation opened.

news.headline: South Africa local elections: ANC 30.76%, DA 24.64%
news.summary: IEC results: the ANC stays the largest party but falls more than 14 points from 2021; Zuma's MK party takes 9.76% in its first local contest.

news.headline: Gunman kills six in Krakow's Main Market Square
news.summary: A 24-year-old man opened fire on 7 Nov, killing six and wounding 15; his parents and sister were found dead at home. He died in hospital on 9 Nov; prosecutors say it is too early to judge any political motive.

news.headline: New Zealand election too close to call
news.summary: Preliminary count: National 42, Labour 36, Greens 16, ACT 13, NZ First 12, Opportunity 7, Te Pati Maori 5 seats. National-ACT-NZ First projected at 67 of 131, a one-seat majority; ~14% special votes remain and final results are due 27 Nov.

news.headline: US added 165,000 jobs in October; unemployment 4.1%
news.summary: Far above forecasts of ~65,000; August and September revised up by 84,000 combined. Fed officials backed further hikes and futures moved toward a December increase.

news.headline: Nikkei 225 plunges more than 7% Friday morning after Wall Street AI sell-off
news.summary: Japan Times: By 10:25 a.m. Tokyo the Nikkei was down 7.09%, falling below 60,000 for the first time since May, tracking Thursday's Nasdaq (−5.5%) and S&P 500 (−4.4%) drop on AI/data-centre regulation fears after the Democratic midterm sweep. Rohm −20%, SoftBank −11%; Topix also down >6% (intraday).

news.headline: Trump weighs three Iran options after NSC meeting; Roosevelt makes Singapore stop
news.summary: Axios: After a post-midterm national-security meeting, Trump said a decision on whether to resume major strikes is coming 'soon' — options include new bombing, continued economic pressure, or a deal with concessions. Qatar mediators circulate a claimed two-day confidence sequence (blockade/funds vs IAEA invite, then Hormuz reopen). CENTCOM is preparing; USS Theodore Roosevelt starts a Singapore port call Friday and is not due in CENTCOM's AOR before mid-November (claims).

news.headline: Child among five killed in Israeli strikes and gunfire across Gaza
news.summary: AFP (Dawn): Gaza civil defence said Israeli strikes and gunfire on Thursday killed five people, including a 12-year-old boy east of Al-Bureij and a woman near Khan Yunis, plus deaths near Al-Zawayda and a drone strike west of Gaza City. IDF said it struck 'terrorists' in Al-Zawayda and west of Gaza City and was looking into the Khan Yunis report. October 2025 ceasefire remains fragile (claims).

news.headline: Delhi's toxic winter air returns as GRAP Stage II and Winter Action Plan take effect
news.summary: BBC: A grey haze and smoky smell returned to Delhi days after the 1 Nov–28 Feb Winter Action Plan began; federal GRAP Stage II restricts diesel generators and coal/firewood burning. Experts welcome earlier planning but say enforcement and regional emissions cuts are still lacking. Winter AQI often exceeds 300 ("very poor").

news.headline: Japan mulls emergency exception to non-nuclear principles in security strategy
news.summary: Kyodo: A government source said Tokyo is considering stating an explicit emergency exception to the three non-nuclear principles in the updated National Security Strategy (due by year-end) — allowing temporary introduction of US nuclear weapons in a contingency — while likely keeping the principles themselves. Reflects Okada 2010 remarks; PM Takaichi has previously questioned the "no introduction" rule. Wording still under LDP–Ishin consultation; China likely to protest (claim).

news.headline: China says DF-61 ICBM has entered Rocket Force routine training
news.summary: CCTV / Global Times: State TV said the DF-61 land-based ICBM, unveiled at the Sept 2025 parade, has been inducted into the PLA Rocket Force and is now used in routine training (field mobility, position changes, launch procedures). No range, numbers or basing disclosed. Expert Shao Yongling said the parade-to-training pace was faster than usual for ICBMs (state-media claim).

news.headline: Trump floats tariffs up to 300% unless foreign firms build US plants
news.summary: Businesskorea / SBS: At the White House on 5 Nov (reported 6 Nov), Trump said foreign companies that do not build US factories could face tariffs from 50% up to 300%, citing >3,000 foreign-owned facilities under construction and arguing tariffs drive the investment. No products, firms or effective date specified — a maximum threat, not a finalized rule (claim).

news.headline: Brent climbs toward $99.86 Friday as Hormuz risks offset de-escalation bets
news.summary: Reuters (Business Recorder): As of 0222 GMT Friday, Brent January futures were about $99.86 (+$1.57 / +1.6%) and WTI about $91.62 (+$1.10). Both gained a second day after Thursday's settle (Brent $98.29). Still on track for ~12% weekly drops after midterm de-escalation bets, but tanker attacks and Hormuz flows under ~60% of capacity (ANZ claim) kept a floor under prices.

news.headline: Zelenskyy: every Ukrainian power plant damaged; seeks Latin America grid help
news.summary: Guardian / agencies: At a Madrid Ibero-American sideline on 5 Nov (briefing 6 Nov), Zelenskyy said every power plant in Ukraine has been damaged 'in one way or another' by Russian attacks and urged Spain and Latin American firms for compatible grid equipment "fast". Overnight exchanges continued; Komyshuvakha toll still cited at 43 with search ongoing.

news.headline: Two Egyptian officers killed in illegal gold-mining crackdown near Sudan border
news.summary: Reuters / Al Arabiya: Military spokesperson said two army officers, including a senior border-guard officer, were killed during the Eastern Desert campaign against illegal gold mining along the Sudan border. Timing of deaths not specified. Campaign (from June) has detained 151 Egyptians and 540 foreigners; phase four due Saturday. Rights monitors previously alleged an Oct airstrike killed miners in northern Sudan — Egypt did not address that claim.

news.headline: NZ election eve: Freshwater poll puts Labour 30.7% ahead of National 26.4%
news.summary: RNZ / The Post: Final Freshwater Strategy poll before Saturday's vote has Labour 30.7% (+2), National 26.4% (−1.2), Opportunity 5.1% (just above the threshold). Right bloc projected ~59 seats vs left ~55 in a 120-seat House; Opportunity would hold the balance if it clears 5%. Other late polls still show a narrow right lead. Polls close 19:00 NZDT Saturday 7 Nov.

news.headline: House Republicans ask Nvidia's Jensen Huang to brief Congress on alleged China spy link
news.summary: CNBC / Axios / House Foreign Affairs: Chairs Mast, Moolenaar and Crawford requested a closed-door joint briefing on 18 Nov about Huang's reported contacts with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang (NYT: alleged PRC intelligence asset) and Nvidia's espionage-security protocols. Reply by 11 Nov. Nvidia says meetings were routine customer contacts and clients get no national-security secrets (claim).

news.headline: Houthis claim drone strike on Dammam airport; coalition says it intercepted missile and drone
news.summary: Xinhua / Al Jazeera: Houthi spokesman Yahya Sarea claimed a drone hit King Fahd International Airport in Dammam and disrupted flights — unverified; no immediate Saudi confirmation. Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed a ballistic missile toward the Medina region and a drone over the Eastern Province. Cross-border exchanges continue as a secondary front of the Iran war.

news.headline: Grynspan extends lead in UNSC straw poll for next UN secretary-general
news.summary: Reuters / The National / Xinhua: In the Security Council's eighth informal straw poll (5 Nov), Costa Rica's Rebeca Grynspan received 12 'encourage' and 3 'discourage' votes, up from 11–4 previously — her strongest showing yet as Guterres's term ends. Which permanent members discouraged her was not disclosed.

news.headline: Japan real wages up 2.2% in September, ninth straight monthly gain
news.summary: CNA / Reuters / Kyodo: Labour ministry data showed real wages +2.2% y/y in September (from revised +1.6% in August); nominal cash earnings +4.6% to ¥311,409 — fastest since Jan 1997. Supports the case for further BOJ rate hikes; many analysts still watch a possible December move.

news.headline: Trump warns US may have to 'destroy the rest' of Iran; decision 'soon'
news.summary: Anadolu Agency / Al Jazeera: In the Oval Office on 5 Nov (reported 6 Nov), Trump said he may have to 'destroy the rest' of Iran and that 'you'll know soon enough', while claiming he would rather not. He also said Iran is 'not doing anything without our approval' when asked about mediator nuclear proposals. Claim — no new strike announced.

news.headline: Iran sends nuclear proposal to US via Qatar; seven preconditions claimed
news.summary: Reuters (via Iran International / Arab News): A senior Iranian official said Tehran sent a nuclear proposal through Qatar but will discuss it only after Washington meets seven demands (sanctions relief, frozen assets, maritime issues among claims). The US is reviewing the offer; details not published.

news.headline: Alliana assumes Paraguay presidency after Peña resigns and is impeached
news.summary: AS/COA / NPR: Santiago Peña resigned on 5 Nov over the Ueno Bank collapse; the lower house then impeached him unanimously. Vice-President Pedro Alliana was spared a parallel impeachment and assumed the presidency; he must manage the bank fallout through August 2028.

news.headline: South Africa local count: ANC 31.8%, DA 24.9% with ~71% counted
news.summary: The Outlier (IEC data): With about 71% of voting districts counted, ANC leads the national PR ballot on 31.8%, DA 24.9%, MK 8.9%. Of 104 local councils decided, ANC won 21 outright, DA 6, MK 3, with 73 hung. Full results still expected around 8 Nov.

news.headline: Putin hosts Iran's Rezaei at the Kremlin on security and postwar arrangements
news.summary: Kremlin / Anadolu: On 5 Nov Putin received Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei, who conveyed a message from Iran's leadership. Talks covered regional security, postwar arrangements and a proposed Russia–Iran gas pipeline (official readout).

news.headline: Massie plans Hegseth impeachment House vote as Congress returns
news.summary: USA Today / WCAX / Roll Call: Rep. Thomas Massie says he will force a House vote on articles of impeachment against Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth when Congress returns (around 9 Nov). Hegseth vowed to fight; Trump still says he is 'doing a very good job'. Removal would still need a two-thirds Senate vote.

news.headline: UNHCR: nearly 90 million displaced people face severe climate risks
news.summary: France 24 / Reuters: UNHCR said on Friday nearly 90 million forcibly displaced people — about three-quarters of the global total — live in countries highly exposed to droughts, floods and extreme heat, urging more adaptation finance ahead of COP31 in Antalya. Only about 10% of climate finance reaches fragile or conflict-affected countries (claim based on UNHCR).

news.headline: Trump says Ukraine war 'very close' to a deal after meeting Putin's envoy
news.summary: DW / AP / Reuters: After a private White House meeting with Kirill Dmitriev (not the Ukrainian delegation), Trump told reporters a 'big, beautiful' agreement is near that 'might involve all of Europe'. He gave no terms; Kushner called Brussels reconstruction/security talks 'productive' ahead of Abu Dhabi 10–11 Nov.

news.headline: Russell Brand convicted of rape and three sexual assaults
news.summary: BBC: A Southwark Crown Court jury found the comedian guilty of one count of rape and three sexual assaults (not guilty on other counts). He was remanded in custody; sentencing is due Monday 9 Nov, with the judge saying to expect a 'significant custodial term'. Met Police say further allegations remain under investigation.

news.headline: Senate Democrats prepare JPMorgan probe over Epstein banking ties
news.summary: CNBC: Democratic staff on the Senate Finance Committee (expected chair Ron Wyden) plan to use subpoena power once they take the majority to examine how JPMorgan handled Jeffrey Epstein, focusing on decisions by asset-and-wealth CEO Mary Erdoes. JPMorgan declined to comment; it has previously said it regrets any association.

news.headline: British Ebola patient arrives at London's Royal Free Hospital
news.summary: Guardian / Reuters: A UK doctor who tested positive while helping the DR Congo outbreak was evacuated and admitted to a specialist isolation unit; authorities say public risk remains low. It is the first British national linked to the current outbreak.

news.headline: Iran reports three more Hormuz tankers damaged after US midterms
news.summary: Reuters: Iran said two tankers struck naval mines and another caught fire on 5 Nov; UKMTO still cites ≥5 vessel incidents since Sunday. Parliament Speaker Qalibaf mocked VP Vance over blaming the Iran war for Republican losses. Qatari mediation continues; no breakthrough announced.

news.headline: North Korea tests new air-defence missile and cruise-missile drill
news.summary: Yonhap/KCNA: Pyongyang said it test-fired a newly designed air-defence missile system on 4 Nov and staged a long-range strategic cruise-missile strike drill against a virtual airport target — its fourth weapons test in a week. South Korea's JCS detected multiple missiles from Sondok flying less than 300 km.

news.headline: Democrats prepare energy and Iran-war probes for January Congress
news.summary: CNBC: With House and Senate control, Democrats plan subpoenas on Trump energy deal-making — Venezuela oil (NABEP), critical-minerals stakes, cancelled renewables — and a war-powers push to end the Iran war. Jeffries said Democrats will 'end this reckless and costly war of choice'.

news.headline: Europe flight hoaxes: emails signed 'fighters of the Male State'
news.summary: Straits Times/AFP: Threat emails to Rome and Sofia airports during the 5 Nov wave of hoax bomb alerts were signed 'the fighters of the Male State'. AFP could not confirm a link to the far-right Russian movement of that name. At least 25–27 flights were disrupted across Europe.

news.headline: France protests revised to 575,000; Lecornu sets Monday social conference
news.summary: France 24: Interior ministry revised Thursday turnout to 575,000 (from ~600,000); CGT still claims nearly 1.6 million. About 448 arrests and 53 injured officers (provisional). PM Sébastien Lecornu will hold a social conference with unions and employers on Monday 9 Nov.

news.headline: Nigerian court voids Atiku's presidential candidacy
news.summary: A Federal High Court in Abuja nullified the David Mark-led leadership of the opposition ADC and all its actions, including Atiku Abubakar's nomination for the 16 January 2027 presidential election. The ADC and Atiku say they will appeal and seek a stay of execution; Atiku calls the timing politically motivated (claim).

news.headline: Nvidia and Qualcomm drop over 9% in post-election chip sell-off
news.summary: CNBC says the Nasdaq fell 5.5%, its worst day since April 2025, as investors priced in a slower AI data-centre buildout after the Democratic sweep; Nvidia lost almost $450bn in market value, AMD, Micron and Applied Materials fell by double digits, and Tesla and SpaceX each dropped more than 9%.

news.headline: Fed's Barkin expects further, gradual rate hikes
news.summary: Richmond Fed President Thomas Barkin said inflation is 'the most important risk' and the Fed will have to raise rates further at a gradual pace. CME FedWatch shows markets pricing a better than 80% chance of a December hike.

news.headline: Newsom to commute all 548 California death sentences
news.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom said he will change every death sentence in the state to life without parole before leaving office. California Supreme Court approval is needed for people convicted of more than one felony.

news.headline: Nithya Raman ousts Karen Bass as Los Angeles mayor
news.summary: Democratic socialist councilmember Nithya Raman, once seen as a long shot, beat the incumbent mayor Karen Bass.

news.headline: Eight killed in a series of shootings in western Turkey
news.summary: Eight people were killed and one seriously injured at several locations in Afyonkarahisar province. Authorities say the suspect fled and was later arrested in Eskişehir province.

news.headline: Myanmar junta intensifies airstrikes in Rakhine
news.summary: France 24 Observers says strikes on 1 Nov killed 12 civilians and injured 32 in Rakhine State, including at a makeshift maternity clinic in Mrauk-U. This is part of the junta's offensive since September to retake the state, which is about 90% held by the Arakan Army. ACLED reports more use of double-tap strikes.

news.headline: Herzog to name who forms Israel's government on Sunday
news.summary: After finishing party consultations, President Herzog said he will announce on Sunday 8 Nov whom he tasks with forming a government. Eisenkot has 67 Knesset recommendations vs Netanyahu's 46; Herzog cited mutual vetoes and will hold private talks with party leaders over the Israeli weekend.

news.headline: Sweden extends Schengen internal border checks citing Russia hybrid threats
news.summary: Government decision: targeted internal border controls from 12 Nov 2026 to 11 May 2027. Justice Minister Gunnar Strömmer (via Reuters) linked the move to sabotage and hybrid threats tied to Russia's war on Ukraine; Kremlin denies the accusations.

news.headline: Italy finalising 13th military aid package for Ukraine
news.summary: Reuters: Defence Minister Guido Crosetto will brief COPASIR on 10 Nov on Italy's first 2026 arms tranche (13th overall). Package may include Aster interceptors for SAMP/T; Crosetto also proposes extending the decree-based aid mechanism beyond 31 Dec 2026 despite League opposition.

news.headline: Russia and Ukraine trade airstrikes as Brussels reconstruction talks resume
news.summary: AP: overnight Russian barrage and Ukrainian drone strikes continued as talks on postwar reconstruction and security guarantees resumed in Brussels. Search continues at Komyshuvakha after Monday's aid-point strike.

news.headline: Burnham: Putin will not be invited to Britain's G20 summit
news.summary: Reuters via Devdiscourse: UK PM Andy Burnham told The Economist that Russian President Vladimir Putin would not be invited to next year's G20 summit in Britain.

news.headline: Putin puts Japan Tobacco's Russian assets under temporary state management
news.summary: A presidential decree transfers JTI stakes in four Russian factories (about 4,000 staff and roughly 40% of the cigarette market) to Industrial Assets / Promyshlennye Aktivy. JTI said it is assessing options; the move follows earlier seizures of Nestle, Auchan, Metro and others.

news.headline: South Korea plans to expand anti-piracy mission closer to Hormuz
news.summary: Seoul will seek Assembly approval to extend the Cheonghae unit from the Gulf of Aden to waters south of Oman (~1,930 km radius), add a P-8A patrol aircraft and an EOD/mine team, and keep operations non-combat and outside the strait itself.

news.headline: Poland detains six over military-parts smuggling to Russia
news.summary: ABW and prosecutors say five Poles and a Russian woman ran a group that moved ammunition and weapons components to Kaliningrad (worth over 2 million zloty). Four face espionage charges and pretrial detention; the group operated at least June 2023-December 2025.

news.headline: Meloni urges EU to appoint a single Ukraine peace envoy
news.summary: In a letter to European Council President Antonio Costa, Italy's PM said overlapping Miami, Oslo, Brussels and other formats make Europe look all over the place and asked for the issue to go on the 13 Nov Dublin informal summit agenda, with a formal decision by December.

news.headline: Nasdaq closes down 5.17% as AI and chip stocks plunge
news.summary: Investing.com historical data put the Nasdaq Composite close at 24,405.73 (-5.17%). Afternoon reporting had the S&P 500 off about 3.7% and the Dow about 2.8-2.9% as chipmakers and data-centre names led a post-midterm AI sell-off.

news.headline: Bank of England raises rates to 4%, first hike in over three years
news.summary: The MPC voted 8-1 to lift Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% (Catherine Mann wanted 4.25%), citing energy prices from the Iran war, and now expects UK inflation near 5% by mid-2027.

news.headline: Eisenkot gets 67 recommendations to form Israel's next government
news.summary: Joint List and Ra'am joined other opposition parties so Eisenkot has 67 Knesset recommendations vs 46 for Netanyahu; UTJ recommended no one. Herzog is expected to grant him the mandate after consultations wrap (28 days, plus up to 14).

news.headline: Melania Trump hosts Russian and Ukrainian officials at the White House
news.summary: The first lady met representatives who arranged the six-day Oleshky ceasefire and called for a more 'enduring' peace, ahead of US-led trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 Nov.

news.headline: Komyshuvakha strike death toll rises to 43
news.summary: Kyiv Independent: 43 bodies recovered after Monday's Russian aerial-bomb attack on an aid point in Zaporizhzhia Oblast; about 33 people still missing. Zelensky called it proof Russia does not want de-escalation as US-hosted talks approach.

news.headline: Joshua Wong jailed for 10 years under Hong Kong security law
news.summary: The pro-democracy activist, due for release in January, was sentenced for colluding with foreign forces under the 2020 national security law.

news.headline: Sudan and Ethiopia expel each other's diplomats
news.summary: Ethiopia ordered six Sudanese diplomats out; Sudan accuses Ethiopia of backing the RSF, while Ethiopia accuses Sudan, Egypt and Eritrea of backing Tigray rebels. Both deny the claims.

news.headline: Developing-country debt hits a record $9.4tn
news.summary: The World Bank's International Debt Report says debt rose 5.5% last year, the fastest in four years, with the poorest countries paying the highest interest rates since the late 1980s.

news.headline: Democrats win control of both houses of the US Congress
news.summary: In the 3 November midterms, Democrats took the House and the Senate in a sharp rebuke of President Trump. Democracy Now reports at least 231 House seats and at least seven Senate pickups, with Mississippi and Alaska still too close to call.

conflicts.name: Russia-Ukraine war
conflicts.latest: US-mediated trilateral talks, the first since February, opened in Abu Dhabi on 10 Nov and run to 11 Nov (Witkoff, Kushner; Medinsky for Russia, Umerov for Ukraine), centred on post-war security architecture; France's Barrot says the UK, Germany and France will be in the room, while a Russian delegation source says a new European security framework is Moscow's main aim. A US official says both sides privately show 'a little bit of flexibility' on territory, which Kyiv publicly denies. Russia keeps striking the power grid while Ukraine hits Russian refineries.

conflicts.name: US/Israel-Iran war
conflicts.latest: Trump told CNN (8 Nov) that renewed strikes are 'highly unlikely' if Iran signs a strong deal on its nuclear programme and Hormuz, but said three carriers are 'locked and loaded' and 38 bridges are targeted. Saxo: he confirmed limited strikes on an air-defence site on Qeshm Island; an Iranian official said there was no damage to vital infrastructure. Rubio called Iran's demands unrealistic; Iran's FM warned of 'hell' if the US chooses war. Ships reported hit near Hormuz; US blockade continues. On 9 Nov Iran said Washington must end sanctions, the blockade and the war before any talks; Araghchi said mediation paused after the US midterms.

conflicts.name: Houthis vs Saudi-led coalition (Yemen)
conflicts.latest: 10 Nov: the coalition said it intercepted two missiles aimed at Riyadh, one towards southern Saudi Arabia and a drone over the Eastern Province. 8 Nov: Saudi defences intercepted Houthi missiles over Riyadh; debris caused limited damage to Aramco's tower in the financial district, no injuries. Houthis claimed strikes on King Khalid airport, Aramco storage tanks and a financial centre (claims). Yemen's army reported heavy fighting against Houthi forces.
conflicts.source: Reuters via Geo News / Al Jazeera / Xinhua

conflicts.name: Gaza
conflicts.parties: Israel, Hamas (Egypt, Qatar, Turkey, US mediating)
conflicts.latest: Axios: Trump asked Netanyahu in a post-election call to move ahead on the Gaza peace plan. Gaza's health ministry says flooding left 350,000 displaced people sleeping in the open; Hamas blamed Israel for a landslide that killed a woman and four children in tents (claim). IDF says it killed two armed men approaching troops.

conflicts.name: Israel-Hezbollah (Lebanon)
conflicts.latest: Israeli shelling, raids and demolitions continued in southern Lebanon despite the ceasefire; Hezbollah claimed drone and missile attacks on Israeli Merkava tanks in response (claims). Herzog says Lebanon talks are among the next government's tasks.

conflicts.name: Sudan civil war
conflicts.parties: Sudanese Armed Forces, Rapid Support Forces
conflicts.latest: IOM: about 2,510 people fled five villages in North Darfur amid worsening insecurity, most into Chad. El Fasher, a year under RSF control, has fewer than 70,000 residents left; RSF drone strikes on power stations deepen outages. Sudan-Ethiopia diplomatic row continues; UN-backed talks with RSF bloc still expected before 25 Dec.

politics.title: US: Massie introduces Hegseth impeachment articles
politics.detail: Eight articles over the Iran war and abuse of power; a House vote could come as early as 11 Nov, with some Republicans signalling support.

politics.title: G7 foreign ministers meet in Paris (9-10 Nov)
politics.detail: Europeans press Rubio to keep Ukraine and Europe in any settlement and to favour diplomacy with Iran; AI safety and maritime security also on the agenda.

politics.title: China: 'in communication' on Trump-Xi-Putin meeting at APEC
politics.detail: Trump says a three-way meeting in Shenzhen (18-19 Nov) is likely; Beijing did not rule it out. Not confirmed.

politics.title: UK: Russell Brand sentenced to 10 years 6 months
politics.detail: For one rape and three sexual assaults; likely to serve two-thirds in custody.

politics.title: Israel: Eisenkot formally tasked with forming a government
politics.detail: 67 recommendations vs 46 for Netanyahu; 28 days plus a possible 14-day extension. He seeks a 'national emergency government'; Netanyahu stays caretaker PM.

politics.title: South Africa: ANC 30.76%, DA 24.64%, MK 9.76%
politics.detail: IEC local election results: ANC still largest but down more than 14 points from 2021.

politics.title: New Zealand: hung result, final count 27 Nov
politics.detail: National 42, Labour 36, Greens 16, ACT 13, NZ First 12, Opportunity 7, Te Pati Maori 5 (preliminary). Luxon runs a caretaker government until final results.

politics.title: US/Iran: Trump weighs strikes, pressure or deal after NSC meeting
politics.detail: Axios: Post-midterm national-security briefing; decision 'soon'. Qatar draft two-day confidence steps circulating (claim). Roosevelt in Singapore Friday; CENTCOM preparing without a new strike directive.

politics.title: Japan: government considers emergency exception to non-nuclear principles in NSS
politics.detail: Kyodo source: updated National Security Strategy may explicitly allow temporary introduction of US nuclear weapons in an emergency while keeping the three principles; wording still under debate.

politics.title: US: Trump floats tariffs up to 300% if foreign firms skip US plants
politics.detail: White House remarks: tariffs of 50–300% threatened for firms that do not build/operate US factories; no product list or effective date — claim, not a finalized rule.

politics.title: China: DF-61 ICBM enters PLA Rocket Force routine training (CCTV)
politics.detail: State TV said the DF-61, unveiled Sept 2025, is now in routine Rocket Force training; no range or deployment figures released.

politics.title: UN: Grynspan leads 8th Security Council straw poll for secretary-general
politics.detail: 12 encourage / 3 discourage for Costa Rica's Rebeca Grynspan — strongest showing in eight closed-door ballots as Guterres's term ends.

politics.title: US: House chairs seek Nvidia Huang briefing on alleged China spy ties
politics.detail: Mast, Moolenaar and Crawford request closed-door session 18 Nov on Alice Huang contacts and Nvidia security protocols; Nvidia calls meetings routine (claim).

politics.title: US: Trump threatens further Iran destruction; decision 'soon'
politics.detail: Oval Office remarks: may have to 'destroy the rest' of Iran; prefers not to; says you'll 'know soon enough'. Asked about mediator nuclear proposals: Iran is 'not doing anything without our approval' (claim).

politics.title: US: Massie plans Hegseth impeachment vote as House returns
politics.detail: Massie says he will force a vote around 9 Nov. Hegseth vows to fight; Trump still backs him publicly. Democrats also preparing Iran-war and energy oversight for January.

politics.title: US/Ukraine: Trump again claims a major peace deal is near
politics.detail: After meeting Dmitriev, Trump said a deal 'might involve all of Europe'. No terms released. Abu Dhabi talks remain 10–11 Nov.

politics.title: Paraguay: Alliana assumes the presidency after Peña exit
politics.detail: AS/COA / Latin Times: Peña resigned and the lower house impeached him 78–0 over Ueno Bank; Alliana was spared a parallel impeachment and assumed the presidency through August 2028. Deposit Guarantee Fund began first reimbursements; Senate trial question remains open.

politics.title: Iran/US: nuclear proposal via Qatar under review
politics.detail: Senior Iranian official (Reuters): proposal sent via Qatar; talks only after seven US concessions (claim). Trump: Iran not acting without US approval.

politics.title: US: Senate Democrats prepare JPMorgan–Epstein banking probe
politics.detail: Finance Committee staff (expected chair Wyden) plan subpoenas focused on how JPMorgan handled Epstein, including decisions by Mary Erdoes.

politics.title: UK: Russell Brand convicted; sentencing Monday
politics.detail: Guilty of rape and three sexual assaults; remanded in custody. Judge said to expect a significant prison term on 9 Nov.

politics.title: US: Democrats prepare energy and Iran-war oversight for January
politics.detail: CNBC: subpoena power on Venezuela oil (NABEP), critical minerals and cancelled renewables; Jeffries pledges a war-powers push to end the Iran war.

politics.title: France: 575,000 protest (ministry); Lecornu sets Monday social conference
politics.detail: Interior ministry revised turnout to 575,000; CGT claims ~1.6 million. PM Lecornu will meet unions and employers on 9 Nov on wages and purchasing power.

politics.title: Europe: hoax bomb threats; 'Male State' claim unverified
politics.detail: ≥25 flights disrupted. AFP saw emails to Rome/Sofia signed 'fighters of the Male State' but could not confirm the Russian far-right group's involvement.
politics.source: The Straits Times / AFP / The Guardian

politics.title: Nigeria: court voids Atiku's ADC presidential nomination
politics.detail: Justice Peter Lifu nullified the Mark-led ADC leadership and its nominations. The ADC will appeal; the election is on 16 Jan 2027.

politics.title: UK: Burnham says Putin not invited to Britain's G20
politics.detail: Asked by The Economist about next year's UK G20 summit, Burnham said Putin would not be invited.

politics.title: Italy: 13th Ukraine arms package; Crosetto to brief COPASIR 10 Nov
politics.detail: First Italian military aid tranche of 2026; Crosetto also proposes extending the decree mechanism past 31 Dec despite League opposition.

politics.title: Sweden: internal Schengen border checks extended to May 2027
politics.detail: Controls from 12 Nov 2026–11 May 2027, citing hybrid threats linked to Russia's war on Ukraine (Kremlin denies).

politics.title: Italy: Meloni presses EU for a Ukraine peace envoy
politics.detail: Letter to Costa calls overlapping formats all over the place and seeks a Dublin (13 Nov) agenda item plus a December decision.

politics.title: Poland: six detained over arms-parts pipeline to Russia
politics.detail: Four charged with espionage; ABW says components including ammunition parts were smuggled toward Kaliningrad.

politics.title: Hong Kong: Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 years
politics.detail: Convicted of collusion with foreign forces under the national security law.

politics.title: US midterms: Democrats take House and Senate
politics.detail: Wins include Senate seats in Texas, Maine, Ohio, North Carolina, South Carolina, Iowa, Kansas and Michigan; Democrats also won a majority of governorships.

politics.title: Israel: results certified, coalition talks begin
politics.detail: Opposition leaders back Gadi Eisenkot. The chosen candidate gets 28 days, extendable by 14; a new election is possible if talks fail.

politics.title: Bulgaria: President Iotova wins a new mandate
politics.detail: Official results gave her 57.58% in the runoff.

politics.title: Spain: cabinet reshuffle before snap election
politics.detail: Transport minister Oscar Puente resigned; Sanchez had called a general election for 29 November.

upcoming.event: Italy: Crosetto briefs COPASIR on 13th Ukraine military aid package
Sweden: renewed internal Schengen border controls take effect (to 11 May 2027)
European Political Community + informal EU Council (Dublin); Meloni wants Ukraine envoy on agenda
EU Foreign Affairs Council (cyberattacks in Europe on the agenda, per Kallas)
Eurostat full euro area inflation data for October
Possible Trump-Xi-Putin meeting on APEC sidelines (not confirmed)
US Federal Reserve rate decision (markets lean toward a hike)
Bank of England next rate decision
UN-backed talks with Sudan's RSF bloc (expected)

economy.detail: Surplus $105.3bn, lowest since April; year-to-date surplus $1.04 trillion.
Forecasts were ~65,000; Aug-Sep revised up 84,000. Average hourly earnings +0.4% m/m. Fed officials backed more hikes.
Producer prices beat the 5.3% forecast, the fastest pace in more than four years; consumer inflation slowed.
Rebounded Monday as the dollar and oil eased; central banks bought 321 tonnes in Q3. Silver ~$52.75.
Ninth consecutive monthly rise; nominal cash earnings +4.6% to ¥311,409 (fastest since Jan 1997). Supports case for further BOJ hikes.
8-1 vote; first hike since Aug 2023. Sees UK inflation near 5% by mid-2027.
Putin decree moves JTI's four Russian factories (~40% cigarette market) to Industrial Assets; JTI assessing options.
10-2 vote; Cook and Hammack wanted a 0.25 point hike. Statement: inflation remains elevated. Barkin (5 Nov) expects gradual further hikes; FedWatch shows a >80% chance of a December hike.
Warned the energy shock is likely to push inflation up and growth down.
8-1 vote; said underlying inflation is now consistent with its 2% target, a first since 2013.
World Bank International Debt Report: up 5.5% last year, fastest rise in four years.
Up from 3.8%. Energy 20.8%; excluding energy, food, alcohol and tobacco 2.5%.
AFP: extending Monday's slide (settled $92.57, -5.85%) after Trump held off new strikes on Iran; WTI ~$85.87 (-1.1%).

Reuters: biggest gain since April as oil slid; Dow +2.21% to 52,417.54, Nasdaq +2.67% to 25,235.49, Philadelphia chip index +6%; Nvidia fell about 5% amid the board probe into CEO Jensen Huang. Brent ~$93 (-4.4%).
DAX +1.89% to 26,282.55, CAC 40 +1.16% to 8,233.30, FTSE MIB +2.69%, FTSE 100 ~+1%. Defence +4.2%, banks +3.1%. Markets price an ECB hike of at least 25bp early next year (LSEG); Sentix fell to 2.4.

Back above 60,000 at the close for the first time in three sessions, led by SoftBank, Advantest and Tokyo Electron; AFP had Kospi +4.1% to 5,223.87, Hang Seng +0.4%, Shanghai +0.3% around the break, tracking Wall Street's rally and lower oil.
Tariff escalation paused, but chip and critical-mineral controls keep growing.
TRM Labs called it the largest crypto theft on record and linked it to North Korea; no government attribution yet.

economyNote: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 November, its first hike in over three years. Japan real wages rose 2.2% y/y in September (ninth straight gain). US payrolls rose 165,000 in October and unemployment fell to 4.1% (CNBC), lifting bets on a December Fed hike. Asian stocks rebounded Monday after last week's AI sell-off, and Brent settled 5.85% lower at $92.57 on Monday and kept falling after hours as Trump played down renewed strikes on Iran (ABC News, citing Reuters). US October CPI is due Tuesday 10 Nov.

history.title: United Nations founded
history.detail: The UN Charter enters into force after the Second World War.

history.title: Cold War begins; India and Pakistan independent
history.detail: The Truman Doctrine sets US containment policy; British India is partitioned.

history.title: State of Israel founded; Berlin Blockade
history.detail: Israel declares independence and the first Arab-Israeli war follows; the Soviets blockade West Berlin.

history.title: NATO formed; People's Republic of China founded
history.detail: Mao Zedong proclaims the PRC; the USSR tests its first atomic bomb.

history.title: Korean War
history.detail: Ends in an armistice that still divides the peninsula.

history.title: Warsaw Pact and Bandung Conference
history.detail: Soviet bloc alliance formed; Asian and African states meet in Bandung, Indonesia.

history.title: Sputnik; Malaya independent; Treaty of Rome
history.detail: Space race starts; the European Economic Community is founded.

history.title: Year of Africa
history.detail: Seventeen African countries gain independence as decolonisation peaks.

history.title: Cuban Missile Crisis
history.detail: The closest the superpowers came to nuclear war.

history.title: Six-Day War; ASEAN founded
history.detail: Israel takes the West Bank, Gaza, Sinai and Golan Heights; five states found ASEAN.

history.title: Yom Kippur War and oil crisis
history.detail: Arab oil embargo quadruples oil prices.

history.title: Fall of Saigon
history.detail: The Vietnam War ends with the country unified under the North.

history.title: Iranian Revolution; Soviet invasion of Afghanistan
history.detail: The Islamic Republic is founded; China begins market reforms under Deng Xiaoping.

history.title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
history.detail: Revolutions sweep Eastern Europe; Tiananmen Square crackdown in China.

history.title: German reunification
history.detail: Iraq invades Kuwait in August; the Gulf War follows in 1991.

history.title: Soviet Union dissolves
history.detail: Fifteen independent states, including Russia and Ukraine, emerge; the Cold War ends.

history.title: End of apartheid; Rwandan genocide
history.detail: Nelson Mandela becomes South Africa's president.

history.title: Asian financial crisis; Hong Kong handover
history.detail: Currency crashes hit Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia and South Korea.

history.title: 9/11 attacks
history.detail: The US launches the war in Afghanistan; China joins the WTO.

history.title: US-led invasion of Iraq
history.detail: Saddam Hussein is overthrown.

history.title: Global financial crisis
history.detail: Lehman Brothers collapses; the G20 becomes the main economic forum.

history.title: Arab Spring
history.detail: Uprisings topple leaders in Tunisia, Egypt and Libya; Syria's civil war begins.

history.title: Russia annexes Crimea
history.detail: War starts in eastern Ukraine; ISIS declares a caliphate.

history.title: Brexit vote and Trump elected
history.detail: The UK votes to leave the EU (exit in 2020).

history.title: COVID-19 pandemic
history.detail: WHO declares a pandemic; the global economy contracts.

history.title: Taliban retake Afghanistan
history.detail: US withdrawal completed.

history.title: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine
history.detail: Largest war in Europe since 1945.

history.title: Hamas attack on Israel; Gaza war
history.detail: Israel launches a war in Gaza.

history.title: Assad falls in Syria
history.detail: Trump wins the US presidential election in November.

history.title: Gaza ceasefire
history.detail: A ceasefire begins in Gaza; second-phase talks are still under way in Nov 2026.

history.title: US and Israel launch war on Iran
history.detail: Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei is killed; the Strait of Hormuz is effectively closed.

history.title: US-Iran memorandum briefly pauses the war
history.detail: It collapses within weeks after renewed attacks on shipping.

history.title: New leaders in Ukraine and the UK
history.detail: Serhii Koretskyi becomes Ukraine's PM (16 Jul); Andy Burnham becomes UK PM (20 Jul).

history.title: Lula re-elected; Israel's election ends in deadlock
history.detail: Neither Israeli bloc reaches 61 seats.

history.title: Democrats win both houses of the US Congress
history.detail: A rebuke of Trump halfway through his second term.

history.title: BoE hike, Paraguay crisis, Europe flight hoaxes, Nasdaq plunge, Trump Ukraine-deal claim
history.detail: BoE lifts Bank Rate to 4%; Peña resigns/impeached over Ueno Bank and Alliana is spared then assumes the presidency; ≥25–27 Europe flights hit by hoax bomb threats (Male State claim unverified); Nasdaq closes −5.17% / Brent settles $98.29; Herzog sets Sunday mandate decision; Melania hosts RU/UA at White House and Trump later claims a major Ukraine deal is near after meeting Dmitriev; Hegseth vows to fight impeachment (Massie aims for a House vote around 9 Nov); North Korea tests new air defence; Russell Brand convicted of rape and sexual assaults; Iranian tankers reported damaged in Hormuz; Putin hosts Iran's Rezaei. A Nigerian court voids Atiku's candidacy.

history.title: Nikkei −7%; Trump Iran decision pending; Gaza ceasefire deaths; Japan nuclear-exception debate
history.detail: Friday morning: Nikkei plunged >7% (Japan Times) after Nasdaq's AI sell-off; Axios said Trump is weighing new Iran strikes, economic pressure or a deal after an NSC meeting, with USS Theodore Roosevelt stopping in Singapore. AFP reported five killed in Gaza including a child amid the fragile ceasefire. Earlier Friday: Kyodo said Japan may write an emergency exception to its non-nuclear principles into the NSS; CCTV said China's DF-61 entered Rocket Force routine training; Trump floated tariffs up to 300%; Brent ~$99.86; Zelenskyy said every Ukrainian power plant has been damaged; Delhi winter smog returned (BBC).

history.title: Eisenkot tasked in Israel; NZ hung result; Krakow shooting
history.detail: Herzog asked Gadi Eisenkot to form a government (8 Nov); New Zealand's election left no clear winner; a gunman killed six in Krakow. Trump called new Iran strikes 'highly unlikely' if talks progress, and Ukraine-Russia-US talks were set for Abu Dhabi on 10-11 Nov.
